name: Replayed
description: A managed service + app where YouTubers upload footage, get matched with a vetted editor, chat, review with timestamped comments and publish. "No subscription" (company-stated).

mentions.evidence: All-time $1,458,751 · L12 $269,754 · L6 $126,885 · L30 $19,911 (−34.3%) MRR shown $3,467 from 1 subscription (most revenue is one-off orders) Monthly: Nov 2025 $27.6k · Dec $28.9k · Jan $19.5k · Mar $23.8k · Jun $15.7k · Sep $32.2k · Oct (partial) $16.2k · founded Feb 2020 Revenue synced 22 October 2026 ~04:05 Warsaw.
mentions.indieAngle: Productised service for a boring B2B output (e.g. "your Allegro listing photos + descriptions done in 24h", or bookkeeping-ready scans) wrapped in a simple upload/review app — the app is the moat, the freelancers are the engine.

whyItPrints: A productised agency with software around it. Not SaaS margins, but six years of steady five-figure months from people who just want edits done.
whyThisMatters:
You upload the footage. A person edits it. You comment on a timestamp and publish. There is no subscription. The company is in the UK and dates to early 2020. The listing calls it a managed service with an app around the matching, the chat, and the review.

Most of the Stripe cash is one-off orders. One subscription shows on the listing, and it is not the business. The months bounce. Some are quieter than the older ones. The all-time total is the long story, six years of people who want the edit done and do not want to hire.

You pay so the video is edited by a person, and the back-and-forth lives in one place.

The softer recent month sits next to older months that were higher. I am not calling that a trend. One month is not the six-year total.

The app is the matching and the comments. The edit itself is still a person.
